1 │ # Black as color number 0 is ignored, and other wrong colors are not reported clearly
   2 │ 
   3 │ ## What happens now
   4 │ 
   5 │ When I choose a color for my text by giving the number 0, which is black, nothing happens. The text shows up with no color at all, and there is no warning that my choice was skipped. The same happens with an empty color value.
   6 │ 
   7 │ Numbers that are outside the allowed range, like 300 or a minus number, are accepted as if they were fine and end up showing nothing useful. The words true and false, when given as a color, are treated as the numbers 1 and 0 instead of being refused.
   8 │ 
   9 │ A color name that is not known does stop with a message that says the color is unknown. But a group of numbers that is the wrong shape, such as only two numbers, four numbers, or three numbers written as text, stops with a confusing internal message about too many values, too few values, or a bad format, instead of saying that the color is unknown.
  10 │ 
  11 │ ## What should happen
  12 │ 
  13 │ The number 0 should show real black for both the text color and the background color.
  14 │ 
  15 │ A value should only be accepted if it is a known color name, a whole number from 0 up to 255, or three whole numbers each from 0 up to 255.
  16 │ 
  17 │ Any other value should stop with one single, clear message that says the color is unknown. That covers empty values, unknown names, text written in capital letters, true and false, minus numbers, numbers above 255, decimal numbers, groups with the wrong count of numbers, and groups that hold text instead of numbers.
  18 │ 
  19 │ ## About this project
  20 │ 
  21 │ Click is a helper library for building command-line programs in Python. It gives people ready-made pieces such as options, prompts, progress bars, and colored output. One of those pieces lets a program put color and style on text it prints to a terminal.
  22 │ 
  23 │ ## Problem this solves
  24 │ 
  25 │ Someone who wants black text or a black background picks the lowest color number and sees nothing happen, so their carefully chosen color is lost without a word. And when they get a color value wrong, the message they see talks about the shape of the numbers rather than telling them plainly that the color is not a real color, which sends them looking in the wrong place.
  26 │ 
  27 │ ## What changed
  28 │ 
  29 │ The number 0 now shows black instead of being skipped, for both text and background.
  30 │ 
  31 │ Bad color values now all stop with the same clear message saying the color is unknown, rather than some being waved through, some being read as a number, and some failing with an internal message about the shape of the numbers.
  32 │ 
  33 │ The kind of error raised for a color that is not known is different from before, so anyone who watches for that specific error should take note.
  34 │ 
  35 │ ## Impact
  36 │ 
  37 │ Ease of use and correctness: a color that was silently dropped now works, and a wrong color now gives one clear message instead of a confusing one. There is also a small compatibility effect on the kind of error raised.
  38 │ 
  39 │ ## User experience
  40 │ 
  41 │ Before: I ask for black text by giving the color number 0 and the text comes out with no color, with no hint that my choice was ignored. After: the same number 0 turns the text black.
  42 │ 
  43 │ Before: I give only two numbers for an RGB color and get a message about not enough values to unpack. After: I get one plain message that tells me the color is unknown.

 324 │     text_or_generator: cabc.Iterable[str] | t.Callable[[], cabc.Iterable[str]] | str,

 399 │ def progressbar(
 400 │     iterable: cabc.Iterable[V] | None = None,
 401 │     length: int | None = None,
 402 │     label: str | None = None,
 403 │     hidden: bool = False,
 404 │     show_eta: bool = True,
 405 │     show_percent: bool | None = None,
 406 │     show_pos: bool = False,
 407 │     item_show_func: t.Callable[[V | None], str | None] | None = None,
 408 │     fill_char: str = "#",
 409 │     empty_char: str = "-",
 410 │     bar_template: str = "%(label)s  [%(bar)s]  %(info)s",
 411 │     info_sep: str = "  ",
 412 │     width: int = 36,
 413 │     file: t.TextIO | None = None,
 414 │     color: bool | None = None,
 415 │     update_min_steps: int = 1,
 416 │ ) -> ProgressBar[V]:
 417 │     """This function creates an iterable context manager that can be used
 418 │     to iterate over something while showing a progress bar.  It will
 419 │     either iterate over the `iterable` or `length` items (that are counted
 420 │     up).  While iteration happens, this function will print a rendered
 421 │     progress bar to the given `file` (defaults to stdout) and will attempt
 422 │     to calculate remaining time and more.  By default, this progress bar
 423 │     will not be rendered if the file is not a terminal.
 424 │ 
 425 │     The context manager creates the progress bar.  When the context
 426 │     manager is entered the progress bar is already created.  With every
 427 │     iteration over the progress bar, the iterable passed to the bar is
 428 │     advanced and the bar is updated.  When the context manager exits,
 429 │     a newline is printed and the progress bar is finalized on screen.
 430 │ 
 431 │     Note: The progress bar is currently designed for use cases where the
 432 │     total progress can be expected to take at least several seconds.
 433 │     Because of this, the ProgressBar class object won't display
 434 │     progress that is considered too fast, and progress where the time
 435 │     between steps is less than a second.
 436 │ 
 437 │     No printing must happen or the progress bar will be unintentionally
 438 │     destroyed.
 439 │ 
 440 │     Example usage::
 441 │ 
 442 │         with progressbar(items) as bar:
 443 │             for item in bar:
 444 │                 do_something_with(item)
 445 │ 
 446 │     Alternatively, if no iterable is specified, one can manually update the
 447 │     progress bar through the `update()` method instead of directly
 448 │     iterating over the progress bar.  The update method accepts the number
 449 │     of steps to increment the bar with::
 450 │ 
 451 │         with progressbar(length=chunks.total_bytes) as bar:
 452 │             for chunk in chunks:
 453 │                 process_chunk(chunk)
 454 │                 bar.update(chunks.bytes)
 455 │ 
 456 │     The ``update()`` method also takes an optional value specifying the
 457 │     ``current_item`` at the new position. This is useful when used
 458 │     together with ``item_show_func`` to customize the output for each
 459 │     manual step::
 460 │ 
 461 │         with click.progressbar(
 462 │             length=total_size,
 463 │             label='Unzipping archive',
 464 │             item_show_func=lambda a: a.filename
 465 │         ) as bar:
 466 │             for archive in zip_file:
 467 │                 archive.extract()
 468 │                 bar.update(archive.size, archive)
 469 │ 
 470 │     :param iterable: an iterable to iterate over.  If not provided the length
 471 │                      is required.
 472 │     :param length: the number of items to iterate over.  By default the
 473 │                    progressbar will attempt to ask the iterator about its
 474 │                    length, which might or might not work.  If an iterable is
 475 │                    also provided this parameter can be used to override the
 476 │                    length.  If an iterable is not provided the progress bar
 477 │                    will iterate over a range of that length.
 478 │     :param label: the label to show next to the progress bar.
 479 │     :param hidden: hide the progressbar. Defaults to ``False``. When no tty is
 480 │         detected, it will only print the progressbar label. Setting this to
 481 │         ``False`` also disables that.
 482 │     :param show_eta: enables or disables the estimated time display.  This is
 483 │                      automatically disabled if the length cannot be
 484 │                      determined.
 485 │     :param show_percent: enables or disables the percentage display.  The
 486 │                          default is `True` if the iterable has a length or
 487 │                          `False` if not.
 488 │     :param show_pos: enables or disables the absolute position display.  The
 489 │                      default is `False`.
 490 │     :param item_show_func: A function called with the current item which
 491 │         can return a string to show next to the progress bar. If the
 492 │         function returns ``None`` nothing is shown. The current item can
 493 │         be ``None``, such as when entering and exiting the bar.
 494 │     :param fill_char: the character to use to show the filled part of the
 495 │                       progress bar.
 496 │     :param empty_char: the character to use to show the non-filled part of
 497 │                        the progress bar.
 498 │     :param bar_template: the format string to use as template for the bar.
 499 │                          The parameters in it are ``label`` for the label,
 500 │                          ``bar`` for the progress bar and ``info`` for the
 501 │                          info section.
 502 │     :param info_sep: the separator between multiple info items (eta etc.)
 503 │     :param width: the width of the progress bar in characters, 0 means full
 504 │                   terminal width
 505 │     :param file: The file to write to. If this is not a terminal then
 506 │         only the label is printed.
 507 │     :param color: controls if the terminal supports ANSI colors or not.  The
 508 │                   default is autodetection.  This is only needed if ANSI
 509 │                   codes are included anywhere in the progress bar output
 510 │                   which is not the case by default.
 511 │     :param update_min_steps: Render only when this many updates have
 512 │         completed. This allows tuning for very fast iterators.
 513 │ 
 514 │     .. versionadded:: 8.2
 515 │         The ``hidden`` argument.
 516 │ 
 517 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 518 │         Output is shown even if execution time is less than 0.5 seconds.
 519 │ 
 520 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 521 │         ``item_show_func`` shows the current item, not the previous one.
 522 │ 
 523 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 524 │         Labels are echoed if the output is not a TTY. Reverts a change
 525 │         in 7.0 that removed all output.
 526 │ 
 527 │     .. versionadded:: 8.0
 528 │        The ``update_min_steps`` parameter.
 529 │ 
 530 │     .. versionadded:: 4.0
 531 │         The ``color`` parameter and ``update`` method.
 532 │ 
 533 │     .. versionadded:: 2.0
 534 │     """
 535 │     from ._termui_impl import ProgressBar
 536 │ 
 537 │     color = resolve_color_default(color)
 538 │     return ProgressBar(
 539 │         iterable=iterable,

 542 │         show_eta=show_eta,
 543 │         show_percent=show_percent,
 544 │         show_pos=show_pos,

 598 │     default the styling is self contained which means that at the end

 600 │     passing ``reset=False``.

 608 │ 
 609 │     Supported color names:
 610 │ 
 611 │     * ``black`` (might be a gray)
 612 │     * ``red``
 613 │     * ``green``
 614 │     * ``yellow`` (might be an orange)
 615 │     * ``blue``
 616 │     * ``magenta``
 617 │     * ``cyan``
 618 │     * ``white`` (might be light gray)
 619 │     * ``bright_black``
 620 │     * ``bright_red``
 621 │     * ``bright_green``
 622 │     * ``bright_yellow``
 623 │     * ``bright_blue``
 624 │     * ``bright_magenta``
 625 │     * ``bright_cyan``
 626 │     * ``bright_white``
 627 │     * ``reset`` (reset the color code only)
 628 │

 630 │ 
 631 │     -   An integer in the interval [0, 255]. The terminal must support
 632 │         8-bit/256-color mode.
 633 │     -   An RGB tuple of three integers in [0, 255]. The terminal must
 634 │         support 24-bit/true-color mode.
 635 │ 
 636 │     See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_color and
 637 │     https://gist.github.com/XVilka/8346728 for more information.
 638 │ 
 639 │     :param text: the string to style with ansi codes.
 640 │     :param fg: if provided this will become the foreground color.
 641 │     :param bg: if provided this will become the background color.
 642 │     :param bold: if provided this will enable or disable bold mode.
 643 │     :param dim: if provided this will enable or disable dim mode.  This is
 644 │                 badly supported.
 645 │     :param underline: if provided this will enable or disable underline.
 646 │     :param overline: if provided this will enable or disable overline.
 647 │     :param italic: if provided this will enable or disable italic.
 648 │     :param blink: if provided this will enable or disable blinking.
 649 │     :param reverse: if provided this will enable or disable inverse
 650 │                     rendering (foreground becomes background and the
 651 │                     other way round).
 652 │     :param strikethrough: if provided this will enable or disable
 653 │         striking through text.
 654 │     :param reset: by default a reset-all code is added at the end of the
 655 │                   string which means that styles do not carry over.  This
 656 │                   can be disabled to compose styles.
 657 │ 
 658 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 659 │         A non-string ``message`` is converted to a string.
 660 │ 
 661 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 662 │        Added support for 256 and RGB color codes.
 663 │ 
 664 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 665 │         Added the ``strikethrough``, ``italic``, and ``overline``
 666 │         parameters.
 667 │ 
 668 │     .. versionchanged:: 7.0
 669 │         Added support for bright colors.
 670 │ 
 671 │     .. versionadded:: 2.0
 672 │     """
 673 │     if not isinstance(text, str):
 674 │         text = str(text)
 675 │ 
 676 │     bits = []
 677 │ 
 678 │     if fg:
 679 │         try:
 680 │             bits.append(f"\033[{_interpret_color(fg)}m")
 681 │         except KeyError:
 682 │             raise TypeError(_("Unknown color {colour!r}").format(colour=fg)) from None
 683 │ 
 684 │     if bg:
 685 │         try:
 686 │             bits.append(f"\033[{_interpret_color(bg, 10)}m")
 687 │         except KeyError:
 688 │             raise TypeError(_("Unknown color {colour!r}").format(colour=bg)) from None
 689 │ 
 690 │     if bold is not None:
 691 │         bits.append(f"\033[{1 if bold else 22}m")
 692 │     if dim is not None:
 693 │         bits.append(f"\033[{2 if dim else 22}m")
 694 │     if underline is not None:
 695 │         bits.append(f"\033[{4 if underline else 24}m")
 696 │     if overline is not None:
 697 │         bits.append(f"\033[{53 if overline else 55}m")
 698 │     if italic is not None:
 699 │         bits.append(f"\033[{3 if italic else 23}m")
 700 │     if blink is not None:
 701 │         bits.append(f"\033[{5 if blink else 25}m")
 702 │     if reverse is not None:
 703 │         bits.append(f"\033[{7 if reverse else 27}m")
 704 │     if strikethrough is not None:
 705 │         bits.append(f"\033[{9 if strikethrough else 29}m")
 706 │     bits.append(text)
 707 │     if reset:
 708 │         bits.append(_ansi_reset_all)
 709 │     return "".join(bits)
